source_lines.31: Input an integer $k\ge1$ and dimension $d\in\{2,3\}$. The coordinate vertices are $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}^d$. Identify them with the zero-based matrix indices $0,\ldots,k^d-1$ by the lexicographic bijection $q(i_1,\ldots,i_d)=\sum_{a=1}^d i_a k^{d-a}$. The grid graph has an edge between two coordinate vertices exactly when they differ by $1$ in one coordinate and agree in all others. Use the graph and ordering conventions of [[def-symmetric-structural-elimination-graph-and-ordering]] on these indices. Thus $d=2$ gives the five-point graph and $d=3$ the seven-point graph.
source_lines.33: Order a rectangular coordinate subbox recursively as follows. For each coordinate whose side length is at least $2$, choose its lower median coordinate, namely the coordinate with $\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor$ positions below it in a side of length $m$. Let $S$ be the union of the coordinate hyperplanes at those selected medians. Delete $S$, obtaining at most $2^d$ nonempty rectangular child boxes. Recursively order the child boxes in lexicographic order of their lower corners, then append the vertices of $S$ in lexicographic order. If no coordinate has side length at least $2$, append the remaining vertex as a terminal separator. Apply this rule first to the whole grid. The resulting order is the **coordinate nested-dissection ordering**.

source_lines.34: Draw one permutation uniformly from all $n!$ permutations of the distinct input sites. Initialize the fixed-universe supertriangle and current triangulation as in [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]], and maintain a directed acyclic graph (DAG) whose leaves correspond one-to-one with current triangulation triangles. Initially the DAG has one leaf for the supertriangle.
source_lines.36: For each next site $p$, start at the root. At each node, order its child triangles lexicographically by their sorted vertex identifiers and test each child by the same three signed-orientation containment tests used by `INSERT` in [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]]. Descend to the unique child containing $p$ until reaching a current leaf $T$. Under the augmented general-position condition, $p$ lies in the interior of a unique triangle at every stage; the located leaf therefore supplies the face certificate `face(T)`. Call `INSERT(p,face(T))` from [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]]. The update verifies that certificate, uses it without a triangle scan, and returns the ordered replacement events. Process those events in order: for a face split, replace the old leaf by pointers to its three new triangle leaves; for an interior-edge split, replace each of the two old leaves by pointers to the two new triangles whose interiors meet that old triangle; for a flip, point each of the two old leaves to both new triangle leaves. Each event names the triangles and overlap map as specified by the insertion procedure. A leaf replaced later is treated in the same way, so the graph remains acyclic and its current leaves correspond exactly to the current triangulation. The insertion procedure also accepts an interior-edge certificate from callers whose admissible inputs permit edge hits; this randomized variant's general-position condition excludes that case. Each internal node has at most three children. After construction, remove synthetic-vertex triangles for the returned Delaunay triangulation; the history DAG is the insertion-time point-location structure.

source_lines.34: **Given:** An integer $k\ge1$, the $k\times k$ nearest-neighbor grid $G_k$, and $A_k=4I-\operatorname{Adj}(G_k)$.
source_lines.36: [F1] [[alg-nested-dissection-ordering-on-regular-grids]]: In dimension two the procedure orders child rectangles first and then appends the union of the selected median row and median column.
source_lines.43: 1.1 For every grid vertex $v$, let $b(v)=4-\deg_{G_k}(v)$ be its number of missing boundary neighbors. Expanding squares gives $$x^TA_kx=\sum_{\{v,w\}\in E(G_k)}(x_v-x_w)^2+\sum_{v\in G_k}b(v)x_v^2.$$ The right side is nonnegative. If it is zero, every adjacent pair has equal coordinates and every boundary vertex with $b(v)>0$ has value zero. The grid is connected and has a boundary vertex, so all coordinates are equal to zero. Hence $A_k$ is positive definite. [given, algebra]
source_lines.45: 2.1 By [F1], the order is the coordinate nested-dissection order on the five-point grid. The matrix is symmetric positive definite by step 1.1 and its off-diagonal pattern is exactly $G_k$. For $k\ge2$, applying [F2] with $n=k^2$ to exact scalar multifrontal Cholesky gives arithmetic work $O((k^2)^{3/2})=O(k^3)$ and symbolic factor storage $O(k^2\log(k^2))=O(k^2\log k)$, with the allocation convention of [F2]. For $k=1$, the matrix and factor each have one entry. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

source_lines.33: Let $n\ge1$, let $r\in\{1,2\}$, and require $n\ge2$ when $r=2$. Let $H_0\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ be upper Hessenberg, and let $P_0$ be a Householder reflector supported on the first $\min(r+1,n)$ coordinates. Set $H_1=P_0^*H_0P_0$. For $j=1,\ldots,J:=\max(n-2,0)$, put $I_j=\{j+1,\ldots,\min(j+r+1,n)\}$. Let $P_j$ be either the identity on $I_j$ or a Householder reflector supported on $I_j$, in either case required to map the active vector $(H_j)_{I_j,j}$ to a multiple of the first coordinate vector, and set $H_{j+1}=P_j^*H_jP_j$. Then $H_{J+1}$ is upper Hessenberg.
source_lines.35: If, in addition, $x\ne0$, $P_0x=\alpha e_1$ with $\alpha\ne0$, and $Q=P_0P_1\cdots P_J$, then $Qe_1=x/\alpha$. Thus the exact chase preserves the initial direction while restoring the Hessenberg zero pattern.
source_lines.51: 1.2 Suppose $\mathcal P(j)$ holds. By hypothesis, the chosen $P_j$ aligns the active vector, including when $P_j$ is the identity. Such choices exist by [F3] for a nonzero vector and by the identity for a zero vector. The below-subdiagonal entries of column $j$ can occur only in rows $j+2,\ldots,\min(n,j+r+1)$, all inside $I_j$. Left multiplication by $P_j^*$ maps the active column segment to a multiple of its first coordinate; here [F2] identifies $P_j^*$ with the reflector $P_j$. The rows beyond $I_j$ already vanish there by $\mathcal P(j)$. Since right multiplication acts only on columns in $I_j$, column $j$ is unchanged by it and is now Hessenberg. If $k<j$, every entry in rows $I_j$ of column $k$ was zero because $i\ge j+1>k+1$; the left update preserves these zeros and the right update does not touch column $k$. Thus columns $k\le j$ are Hessenberg after this step. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]
source_lines.53: 2.1 The left update changes only rows at most $j+r+1$. In the columns in $I_j$, any entry below the first subdiagonal in a row greater than $j+r+2$ is zero before the right update: it lies below the Hessenberg band, and its row exceeds the support bound in $\mathcal P(j)$. The right update mixes only columns in $I_j$, so those entries remain zero. In columns outside $I_j$, the right update makes no change; rows outside the left support are unchanged, and every below-subdiagonal entry in a row greater than $j+r+2$ was already zero by $\mathcal P(j)$. Therefore every below-subdiagonal entry of $H_{j+1}$ lies in a row $i\le\min(n,j+r+2)$, proving $\mathcal P(j+1)$. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

source_lines.44: [F2] [[lem-nested-dissection-fronts-are-boundary-limited]]: For the full grid and a vertex in the separator of a box of side at most $s$, its factor-column size $d_v=\ell_v+1$ is at most $3d s^{d-1}$.
source_lines.53: 1.1 If a box side has length $m\ge2$, the median rule leaves each child side with length at most $\lceil m/2\rceil$; a side of length $1$ stays $1$. Iterating gives side lengths at depth $r$ at most $s_r=\lceil k/2^r\rceil$. There are at most $2^{dr}$ boxes at that depth because each box has at most $2^d$ children. By depth $R=\lceil\log_2 k\rceil$, every side has length $1$, so all remaining boxes are terminal. For $0\le r\le R$, $k/2^r\ge1/2$, hence $s_r\le2k/2^r$. [F1, induction, algebra]
source_lines.57: 1.3 Let $G'$ be the structural graph of $A$ and let $G$ be the full nearest-neighbor grid on the same vertices. They use the same coordinate ordering. If a pair is an edge in a filled graph of $G'$, [F3] supplies a witness walk in $G'$ with internal vertices eliminated earlier; since $G'$ is a subgraph of $G$, the same walk witnesses that edge in the corresponding filled graph of $G$. Thus every later filled neighbor in $G'$ is also one in $G$, and each subgraph column size is at most the full-grid column size. Fix a box at depth $r$. Its separator has at most $d s_r^{d-1}$ vertices by the union bound over its at most $d$ median hyperplanes; the terminal singleton satisfies the same bound. By [F2], each such pivot has full-grid column size at most $3d s_r^{d-1}$, so the same bound holds for $A$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]
